clue.text: As bore, inclined somehow to be petty

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: A tiresome person who is inclined to be small-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little size or importance is trivial, the same sense as petty.

clue.text: Vehicle running over ram creates disturbance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece runs over, that is above, the second

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A vehicle knocking down a ram causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or brawl is a commotion, a kind of disturbance.

clue.text: Good guy enthralling listeners disappears in a hurry

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a toff is a well-to-do gentleman, a fine fellow
ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: A hero who has his audience spellbound suddenly vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh or upper-class man.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush away is to dash off at speed, so the phrase is an idiom for leaving hurriedly.

clue.text: Grounds may be abandoned after this social event

definitions.text: Grounds may be abandoned after this social event

parts.words: Grounds may be abandoned after this social event
parts.note: grounds suggests sports fields left empty, but it is the coffee dregs left behind after a morning gathering

explanation.surface: A sports ground left deserted after some party.
explanation.walkthrough: A British coffee morning is an informal gathering, often for charity, where coffee is served; the grounds left over are the used coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A daytime social gathering over hot drinks, commonly held in Britain to raise money for charity.

clue.text: Land-holder is woman (or man) keeping donkey

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: Val is a name for either sex, short for Valerie or Valentine

explanation.surface: A landowner, either female or male, who keeps a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a vassal held land from a lord in return for service and loyalty.

clue.text: Lady's block on letter being spelt out

parts.note: the letter S written out in full is ess

explanation.surface: A woman's barrier set upon a letter written in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a peerage title is addressed as Lady, the rank equal to a baron.

clue.text: Sort of word to encapsulate chaps getting old — something not sensed

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so one piece surrounds others

parts.note: a noun is a type of word

explanation.surface: Some type of word enclosing ageing fellows names a thing beyond perception.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kant's philosophy a thing-in-itself, known by reason rather than through the senses.

clue.text: Dish mum offered with endless healthy stuff?

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word

parts.note: a salad is a healthy meal

explanation.surface: Mother serves a meal alongside something wholesome, minus its final part.
explanation.definitionFit: A curry or blend of spices served as an Indian meal, a dish in itself.

clue.text: Lecture that may involve use of otoscope and syringe

definitions.text: Lecture that may involve use of otoscope and syringe

parts.words: Lecture that may involve use of otoscope and syringe
parts.note: a sharp telling-off is a reproof, and an insect lodged in the ear might need a doctor's otoscope and syringe

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a scolding is read literally as a bug in someone's ear, which a doctor would examine and flush out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a sharp scolding or rebuke, the reproving sense of a lecture.

clue.text: Straightforward in a way that our crossword isn't!

definitions.meaning: clear-cut, with no shades of grey

definitions.text: in a way that our crossword isn't!
definitions.meaning: the FT is printed on pink paper, so its crossword is not merely monochrome

explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is famous for its salmon-pink newsprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut, with no grey areas, is spoken of as monochrome both literally and in idiom.

clue.text: Animal fashioned by craftsperson without head

indicators.note: without head means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a potter is a craftsperson who makes pots

explanation.surface: A creature carved by an artisan, but it lacks a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eating river mammal with webbed feet, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Item of church furniture ruined by last flood

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A piece of church furnishing wrecked by the most recent deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding stool or desk used by a bishop or for prayer, a piece of church furnishing.

clue.text: Guess attitude will be evident after drink

indicators.note: after places the attitude piece following the drink piece

parts.note: a pose is an attitude, a stance

explanation.surface: A speculation that a person's demeanour will show itself once they have had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess is to assume or presume, the verb sense of conjecture.

clue.text: Big hole in rock article produced by sculptor

parts.note: Alexander Calder was an American sculptor known for mobiles

explanation.surface: A sculptor creates an object with a large hole in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A large basin-shaped crater formed when a volcano collapses, a huge hollow in rock.

clue.text: Female appearing on stage means floorboard may come loose

indicators.note: coming loose suggests the pieces are freed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress on stage, which means a board in the floor might work free.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Flora Robson was a celebrated twentieth-century English actress of stage and screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished British actress made a Dame, so a woman who appeared on stage.

clue.text: Muttering when the old woman has tacky jewellery

parts.note: the old woman is slang for one's mother, mum

explanation.surface: Mother grumbles under her breath while wearing cheap jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking indistinctly and low is muttering, a close synonym.

clue.text: Scot able to get drunk in bar

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who can get drunk in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier or hindrance blocks the way, as a bar does.

clue.text: Fast tram — a danger not all spotted

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is seen, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: A speedy tram is a hazard that not everyone notices.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month during which believers abstain from food in daylight hours.

clue.text: Two words to indicate fantastic ruin

explanation.surface: A remark that two words suggest wonderful destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like a comment on the clue, but it is a literal instruction: find two slang words for fantastic.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil the look of something by damage or marking is to ruin it.

clue.text: Haughtiness that makes one criticise European out loud

parts.note: dis is slang for criticise, disrespect

indicators.note: out loud means the word is spoken, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: Arrogance that leads one to say bad things about a continental, openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt or scorn for those thought beneath one, a form of haughtiness.

clue.text: Stories about drink producing medical condition

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ana are collections of anecdotes or stories

explanation.surface: Tales of boozing that lead to illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chest pain from reduced blood flow to the heart, a recognised medical condition.

clue.text: Bird group traversing lakes starts to fly inland

indicators.note: traversing means lying across, so one piece spans the others inside it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, doubled for lakes

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A flock of birds crossing lakes begins to head inland.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch with a pink breast and black cap, a common European songbird.

clue.text: Guardian contends leader of Egypt must go

indicators.note: must go means that letter is removed
leader of picks the opening letter of the word after

explanation.surface: A protector argues that Egypt's ruler should step down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a hundred-eyed giant set as watchman, so a vigilant guardian.

clue.text: Woman from French city assigned to organisation based in Brussels

parts.note: the EU, European Union, has its headquarters in Brussels
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A woman from a French city posted to the Brussels bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman, as crosswords often define names.

clue.text: A state capital imprisons fast woman

indicators.note: imprisons means locks up, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A US capital city jails a promiscuous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast woman' suggests promiscuity, but it is literal: in Greek myth the huntress was a swift runner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek huntress who would marry only a man who outran her, famed for speed.
